introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

(Sections: A Map Work, B Physical Geography, C Human Geography, D Cameroon Geography. Question 1 is the only question of Section A.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) On the outline map of Cameroon provided, **locate** and **name** the following:

(i) A main River. (ii) One area of dense population

(iii) One area of sparse population. (iv) The Adamawa Plateau.

(v) An area of dense vegetation cover.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The outline shows only the border of Cameroon with the north arrow: the southern border is at about 2 degrees N, the Atlantic coast is in the south-west (about 4 degrees N) and the northern tip (Lake Chad) is at about 13 degrees N. Mark each feature and write its name beside it.

**(i) A main river:** the **River Sanaga**, which rises on the Adamawa Plateau (centre of the country) and flows south-west and west to the Atlantic Ocean near Edea, south of Douala. (Other main rivers: the Benue in the north, flowing west into Nigeria; the Wouri at Douala; the Nyong and the Ntem in the south; the Logone in the far north.)

**(ii) An area of dense population (one):** the **Western Highlands** (Bamenda and Bafoussam areas, in the west), or the **Douala-Wouri coastal area**, or the **Yaounde** area in the centre-south; also the Mandara Mountains and Maroua in the far north.

**(iii) An area of sparse population (one):** the **East Region** (the south-eastern forest and its border with the Central African Republic), or the **Adamawa Plateau and the south-eastern forests** in general.

**(iv) The Adamawa Plateau:** in the **centre of the country**, in the "waist" between the northern plains and the southern plateau, at about **6 to 8 degrees N** (Ngaoundere is on it); it stretches roughly east-west at 1 000 to 1 500 m above sea level.

**(v) An area of dense vegetation cover:** the **equatorial rainforest** of the **south and south-east** (south of about 5 degrees N, towards the borders with Gabon and Congo); the mangrove along the coast is also accepted.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Outline **six** tourist resource facilities of the country.

(3 marks)

(ii) Briefly describe **TWO** measures the government has used to promote tourism and leisure in the country.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Six tourist resource facilities of Cameroon.**

1. **National parks and game reserves** such as Waza, Benoue and Korup (wildlife and rainforest).
2. **Beaches** on the Atlantic coast, such as Kribi and Limbe.
3. **Mount Cameroon** (an active volcano) and the **Mandara Mountains** for hiking and scenery.
4. **Waterfalls and lakes**, such as the Ekom and Lobe waterfalls and the crater lakes of the western highlands.
5. **Cultural attractions:** chiefdoms and palaces (such as the Foumban palace), museums and traditional festivals.
6. **Hotels, restaurants and airports** that welcome visitors.

**(ii) Two measures used by the government.**

1. **Creating a body in charge of tourism and leisure:** the government set up a **Ministry of Tourism and Leisure** to plan, manage and promote the sector, to classify hotels and to protect the tourist sites (national parks and reserves).
2. **Promotion and development of facilities:** advertising Cameroon ("Africa in miniature") through brochures, websites and tourism fairs, organising festivals, and improving roads, airports and hotels, with training of hotel and guide staff, so that more visitors come.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Suggest to the government what should be done to improve on her:

(i) Trade with other countries

(ii) Agricultural output.

(4 + 4 = 8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) To improve trade with other countries.**

1. **Process raw materials before export** (cocoa, coffee, cotton and timber) to earn more from each tonne and to export manufactured goods.
2. **Improve roads, railways, ports and border posts** (for example the Douala and Kribi deep-sea ports) so goods move quickly, cheaply and without delays or corruption.
3. **Diversify exports and markets** and sign trade agreements with neighbouring countries (CEMAC and the African continental free trade area), so that Cameroon does not depend on a few products.
4. Improve the **quality of Cameroonian products** to meet international standards and encourage "made in Cameroon" goods.

**(ii) To improve agricultural output.**

1. **Provide improved seeds, fertilisers and equipment** at low prices (subsidies) and encourage mechanisation.
2. **Give credit to farmers** through agricultural banks and micro-finance, and support farmers' cooperatives.
3. **Build feeder roads, storage barns and processing factories** so that farm produce reaches the market and does not rot.
4. **Train farmers** through extension workers and research, and develop irrigation in the dry north.
